header: Gold answers for 20 callable people, used by `python -m eval.check_people` to score outputs/*/people.json and outputs/*/ranked.json.

HOW THIS GOLD WAS BUILT. (1) Which people: chosen by the fixed rule in 'selection_rule', from the pipeline's own ranked call lists. The rule uses only rank order and list length. It was written after the names and displayed amounts of the call lists had been seen, but before any source page was read, and it does not look at whether the pipeline got anyone right.

(2) What is right: every value below was read from the printed source pages, not copied from the pipeline's outputs. Pages were read as text from the cached copy of each PDF (cache/pages) and again with a second extractor (pdftotext -layout on cache/fetch/<sha>.bin). Page images were looked at for the scanned or two-column pages (Spacenet pdf pages 3 and 6; FDC page 1). Every field carries pdf_index, printed_page where the page prints one, and a short quote. `python -m eval.check_people --verify-gold` re-checks that each quote is on its page (spaces and case ignored) and that each expected amount equals shares x price.

(3) Who read them: an AI assistant (Claude) in one session, not a human analyst. It is a careful second reading, not an independent audit. The pipeline's page locator was used only to learn which documents to open; the numbers were taken from the pages. Please spot-check a few rows against the PDFs.

Second-extractor check covered every page cited in this file: HD Fire pdf 1, 10, 106, 108, 109, 110, 387; SFC 13, 87, 158, 163, 585; Tonbo 1, 3, 129, 477; SEDEMAC RHP 20, 21, 22, 132, 133 and the allotment ad pages 1, 2; Spacenet 2, 3, 6, 8; FDC page 1. The check was on the key numbers and sentences, not every word of every page.

WHAT THE SCORE DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. The 20 people come from the pipeline's own call lists, so the score measures how correct the pipeline is on people it called. It does not measure people it missed (recall against all sellers and holders in each document). Top-ranked people are probably easier than the long tail. The two picks the rule skipped and that look like misses are named in 'skipped_by_rule' so the number is not flattered silently.

Amounts are what the printed numbers give: shares offered x the printed price (gross, before fees, taxes and the employee-portion discount). A seller's amount is cash; a holder who is not selling gets the value of the shares at the offer price, not cash. A person whose own share count or price is not printed has amount kind 'not_printed': the right output is 'unknown', and a number there counts as invented.

Dates marked derived are computed from printed rules (lock-in months from an 'on or about' allotment date; settlement days from an offer date). They are estimates of the same kind the pipeline makes. A person whose listing/allotment date is only the timetable's 'on or about' is scored on that printed date.
Gold values are as of the documents in cache/fetch; the call lists will change when the pipeline is re-run, which is why people are matched by printed name, not by rank.
selection_rule: For each of the six events below, take the top 3 people by rank in the event's ranked.json 'callable' list (3 x 6 = 18). Add 1 extra person to each of the 2 events with the most callable people (SFC 22, SEDEMAC 19), picked at 0-based list position 3 + (int(sha256(event_id), 16) mod (callable_count - 3)). That gives 20. Events: every processed event that is an IPO/OFS with at least 3 callable people and a source document with printed per-person numbers, plus the one buyback with named promoters; the other processed events had 0-1 callable people or were not read for this gold.

skipped_by_rule.would_have_been: extra pick at list position 7 (rank 8): CEAQ India, an investor selling shareholder; the call list showed amount unknown. Not sampled because Tonbo is not one of the two largest lists.
extra pick at list position 4 (rank 5): Anik Narendra Dharamshi, a promoter; the call list showed no role. Not sampled for the same reason.
